claims.text: AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake and supersede an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, so the waiting execution is dropped before it starts.
If a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued CodePipeline execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each runs in turn rather than being superseded by a later execution.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` for a CodePipeline pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is documented at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ and is described further below in the page.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict error.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment, which can prevent concurrent runs of a deployment job that targets that environment.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level property that controls how a stage behaves with respect to an exclusive lock check on an environment it references.
The default value of the Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` stage property is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
`lockBehavior: sequential` runs every queued stage against the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud itself serializes updates to a stack, one at a time, in the same way `sequential` lock behavior does.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `command: up` running an update.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one run.
When two concurrent runs target the same Pulumi stack, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
The page links to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ as the page describing update conflicts.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', located under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0, meaning unlimited.
Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 causes a second build to be queued behind the first and run only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud applies a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior.
In Azure Pipelines, an exclusive lock check added to the environment that a deployment job targets serializes Pulumi deployments.
Azure Pipelines supports a `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on a stage, which makes runs wait in sequence for the exclusive lock.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored '#serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
AWS CodePipeline pipelines have an execution mode setting, and setting it to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section anchored '#serialize-pipeline-executions'.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', and setting it to 1 prevents concurrent Pulumi deployments.
The Pulumi TeamCity guide at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section anchored '#limit-concurrent-builds' describing this setting.
